If you import full containers from China and receive a U.S. demurrage or detention invoice, start with one container and the exact days charged. Match the invoice to your agreed free time, then compare those dates with the terminal’s pickup records and the trucker’s equipment interchange receipts. If a billed day falls after a confirmed empty return, ask the invoice issuer to correct that line and attach the return receipt. Save the filing deadline as soon as the invoice arrives. You can collect the supporting records while you prepare the request.

  • Confirm which company issued each charge and whose tariff or contract it applied.
  • Rebuild the charged days with terminal and trucking records.
  • Submit the disputed dates, supporting documents and requested correction to the invoice issuer.

Check who billed you and which clock they used

For a typical separate-clock import bill, demurrage concerns a container still at the terminal after free time. Detention concerns equipment kept outside the terminal after its free time, usually until the empty is accepted at the designated return location. Some quotes combine the clocks. Start with the wording in your service contract or applicable tariff and the item shown on the bill.

Check whether the issuer is the ocean carrier, the terminal or a non-vessel-operating common carrier (NVOCC). If your forwarder sends a summary, ask which company assessed the charge and request the underlying invoice or an itemized breakdown. Keep terminal storage, inland rail storage and trucking wait time on their own lines. The amount alone tells you little about which terms apply or which company can correct it.

Rebuild the charge day by day

Find the free-time allowance that applies to that container, its start event, and how the tariff counts weekends and holidays. Pull the terminal’s availability and last free day records. Get the out-gate receipt and empty-return receipt from the drayage provider. If the pickup or return location changed, keep the original instruction, the revision and their timestamps.

Suppose the invoice lists September 13–15 as detention days. Your trucker’s equipment interchange receipt shows the same empty container was accepted at the authorized depot on September 14. Ask the issuer to explain September 15 and review the September 14 cutoff under the applicable terms. Attach the receipt with the container number, depot and timestamp visible. If the carrier’s record shows a different return date, ask it to identify the event it used before recalculating the charge.

Appointment screenshots are most useful when they show the relevant container, facility, date and available slots or rejection message. Check the issuer’s evidence instructions as soon as a return is blocked. For example, Maersk’s U.S. instructions for empty-return appointment disputes specify local-time windows for screenshots and require an email requesting an alternate return location before the first date in the waiver request. If a terminal closure or return restriction blocked movement, save the notice and record when you tried again. Ask how the issuer treated those exact dates. The FMC’s interpretive rule considers whether a charge could serve its purpose of encouraging cargo movement and equipment return, including when returning an empty was impossible.

Demurrage and detention invoice checklist

CheckEvidence to pullWhat to ask the issuer
Invoice and containerInvoice number, bill of lading and container numberConfirm the issuing company, charge type and shipment reference.
Free time and rateService contract or applicable tariff, equipment type and last free dayIdentify the rule, free-time start and daily rate tiers used.
Pickup and empty returnTerminal availability record, out-gate and empty-return receiptsReconcile the first and last charged days with the recorded events.
Blocked pickup or returnAppointment attempts, closure notices and depot instructionsReview the specified dates and explain how access restrictions were treated.
Invoice and request datesInvoice issue date, last day charged, upstream invoice if the issuer is an NVOCC, and submission receiptConfirm the applicable issuance and request dates, then acknowledge the case.

File with the issuer and keep the case number

Use the dispute channel shown on the invoice or the issuer’s current instructions. Send the invoice and container numbers, the line items and dates you challenge, a short explanation, the relevant evidence and the adjustment you seek. For example, ask the issuer to remove September 15 and send a revised invoice. Keep the portal confirmation or acknowledgment email with your copy. Maersk directs customers to MyFinance or its disputes email for post-pickup U.S. demurrage disputes. CMA CGM lists its own invoice dashboard, customer service portal and disputes contact.

For invoices covered by 46 CFR Part 541, the billing party generally has 30 calendar days from the last day the charge was incurred to issue the invoice. An NVOCC has a separate 30-calendar-day issuance rule measured from the issue date of the invoice it received. The billed party must be allowed at least 30 calendar days from the issue date of the invoice it is contesting to request mitigation, a refund or a waiver. The billing party must attempt to resolve that request within 30 calendar days of receiving it, unless both sides agree to a later date.

The court set aside § 541.4, which had specified who could be invoiced. Section 541.6 still requires a covered invoice to explain why the issuer considers you liable. Check that explanation against the contract and shipment records. If an issue with a common-carrier charge remains unresolved and you believe it violates the Shipping Act, review the FMC’s current Charge Complaint procedures and keep your invoice, bill of lading and correspondence together.

Ask DDNZ about China–US full-container freight. Send the origin, U.S. port, container type and planned pickup or return arrangement. If a previous charge is relevant to the next booking, share a redacted invoice and the dates you want to check.

Frequently asked questions

Which date should I use to track my request deadline?

For a covered invoice, start with its issue date and check the issuer’s terms for any longer period. Submit through the listed channel and save the acknowledgment.

What if the invoice leaves out the applicable rate or dispute contact?

Identify the missing fields and request a complete invoice in writing. Part 541.5 ties payment obligation to the required information in § 541.6 for covered invoices. Keep the original and track your request from the original issue date while you seek clarification.

Can I dispute days when I could not book an empty return?

Document each attempt, including the specified depot, available slots or rejection message, and any revised return instruction. Ask the issuer to review the affected dates against those records.
